items.title: phpAfterShell Explained: How Hackers Could Turn a PHP Session Flaw Into Code Execution
items.description: PHP's default file-based session storage can be made to return objects an attacker chose, by cutting off a session write at the right moment. When combined with a second weakness, such as a suitable gadget chain in the app, those objects can allow the attacker to run code on the server. items.description: A critical flaw in VMware vCenter lets an attacker with network access bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system, Broadcom, which owns VMware, said in an advisory published today. items.title: Five warning signs of ransomware breach before encryption or data theft
items.description: Ransomware attacks often involve credential theft, lateral movement, and attempts to disable security controls long before encryption begins. Acronis examines five warning signs that can help defenders detect intrusions earlier, contain malicious activity, and protect critical systems and backups. [...]

items.title: Critical NGINX ‘NGINX2Root’ bugs let attackers hijack servers
items.description: Two critical NGINX vulnerabilities dubbed "nginx2root" allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code remotely on vulnerable web servers, with researchers demonstrating how the flaws can be chained with a Linux kernel bug to gain root access. [...]

items.title: Drupal Patches Critical Installer Flaw That Could Give Unauthenticated Attackers Control of Sites
items.description: Under specific conditions, a critical vulnerability in Drupal core can allow an attacker without login credentials to use the built-in installer to attempt to reinstall a site. That can lead to a site takeover or remote code execution, and the project rates the vulnerable configurations as uncommon. Fixed releases for all supported branches shipped yesterday. items.title: Everything Is a Web Application, Including Your Firewall
items.description: One of the early targets of PHP2Shell exploitation was the firewall. On October 28, Palo Alto Networks confirmed that attackers were exploiting the two PHP vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet. Both flaws let anyone execute code on the web server without authentication. The disclosure itself went a little wrong.
